HRX hardware gate#

ci.yml runs on a GitHub runner with no GPU, so it cannot see an HRX kernel or pin that computes the wrong thing. Eight HRX correctness bugs were found by hand within ten days: #308, #309, #310, #313, #318, #319, #369 and #370. The hardware gate checks every HRX pin bump, and every PR that asks for it, on the Strix Halo box before merge.

When it runs#

.github/workflows/hw-gate.yml, job hw_gate, on the self-hosted runner strixhalo-engine:

  • A labelled PR. Add the label hw-gate to a PR from this repository. Adding the label starts the job, and every later push runs it again.
  • Every PR that bump-hrx opens (branch bump-hrx/*).
  • By hand. Actions -> hw-gate -> Run workflow, with a ref (a branch, tag, SHA or pull/N/head). The run posts the commit status hw-gate on the commit it checked, so a PR shows the result.

A pin bump raised by hand must therefore do one of the two automated things: name its branch bump-hrx/<sha> (the bump-hrx workflow's own convention) or add the hw-gate label. Neither is a formality - without one the job does not run and the PR simply reads hw_gate: skipping, which looks like a pass in a list of ticks (engine#672: a hand-raised llama.cpp bump on a 1bit/bump-hrx-<sha> branch went to merge with no gate status until the label was added; the gate then ran normally).

PRs from forks never run there: the runner is the owner's box.

What it checks#

scripts/hw-gate.sh builds this checkout's HRX pair (third_party/llama.cpp and third_party/hrx-system) with the configuration of cmake/hrx.cmake, plus test-backend-ops and llama-perplexity, with the private HIP kernels compiled in as the release builds them: the private add-on at the commit the release config pins, fetched by the private-fetch helper with the runner box's gh login and passed as GGML_HRX_HIP_ADDON_DIR. A llama.cpp pin and an add-on pin that do not compile together fail the build step (2026-10-20: an add-on pin used a kernel-side type the pinned llama.cpp did not have yet), and so does a build whose libggml-hrx.so lacks the add-on. A box that cannot read the add-on stops with exit 2; HW_GATE_PRIVATE=0 gates the public plumbing only. On a failed build the job log shows the compiler's error lines without their source excerpts, since the log is public and the add-on's sources are not. It then runs six checks:

check what catches
ops one test-backend-ops -b HRX0 -j 4 run over MUL_MAT, MUL_MAT_ID, FLASH_ATTN_EXT, GATED_DELTA_NET, SSM_CONV, GET_ROWS, ROPE, RMS_NORM, SOFT_MAX a kernel that disagrees with the CPU (#310, #313, #370, the IQ ports)
fa-decode-q8 the add-on's own long-context decode-attention check against a double-precision reference, quantised K with both cache value types and two head groupings, six runs in one hold a mixed cache-type bug test-backend-ops cannot see: it has no FLASH_ATTN_EXT case with K and V of different types
kat tools/kat.py check on five models (below), against tests/golden/hw-gate/kat-<model>.json wrong answers, empty replies, NaN logprobs, nondeterminism, cached-prefix and multi-ubatch bugs, drift from the release pin (#308, #309, #315, #318, #319, #369)
kld llama-perplexity --kl-divergence on wiki.test.raw, 512 tokens x 8 chunks, against base logits stored at the release pin small numeric drift that greedy answers do not show
needle tests/hrx_long_prompt.py: the 320-record vault-code needle (7.1K tokens on Qwen3, 7.4K on ZAYA1) on Qwen3-0.6B and ZAYA1-8B #319, #369
placement every graph the server scheduled for each model (load, warmup, the kat prompts, the needle) is all on HRX, read from ggml-hrx's placement report a pin that leaves a node on the CPU, which 1bit serve now refuses to load by default (1bit serve)

The models (MODEL_TABLE in the script, files under ~/models):

name file covers kat repeats needle
qwen3-0.6b Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_K_M.gguf small dense K-quant 3 yes
zaya1-8b zaya1-8b-Q4_K_M.gguf ZAYA1 (16 experts, 1 active per token), K-quant 2 yes
qwen3.8-27b qwen38/UD-Q4_K_XL/Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf gated delta net + attention hybrid, Unsloth dynamic mix 2 no
qwen3-coder-30b-a3b Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf qwen3moe: 128 experts, 8 active per token (MUL_MAT_ID with top-8 routing) 2 no
qwen3-4b-iq4xs Qwen3-4B-IQ4_XS.gguf an IQ quant (IQ4_XS matmul and GET_ROWS) 2 no
qwen3-0.6b-kq8 Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_K_M.gguf, served with -fa on -ctk q8_0 a q8_0 K cache with an f16 V cache 2 yes
qwen3-0.6b-kvq8 Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_K_M.gguf, served with -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 q8_0 K and V caches 2 yes

The last two rows give llama-server extra arguments (the fifth column of MODEL_TABLE). Their kat needle (about 4.7K tokens) and the 7.1K-token needle decode past 1,024 KV cells, where the add-on's split decode kernel (fa_decode_q8_d128) takes over from its prompt kernel; the short kat cases decode through the prompt kernel with one query. Both bugs of gpu-kernels #11 showed only on that path: a launch parameter registered on the wrong kernel (every long decode failed with "compiled ABI does not match manifest", HTTP 500) and an f16 V read that covered dims 0..31 only. The rows run kat, the needle and placement but not kld, since a KLD base is stored per model file and recorded with the default f16 cache.

kat repeats every case and fails on any of: - a missing expected answer; - an empty reply or a NaN logprob; - two different texts for the same request; - text that leaves the golden before token 8; - a logprob more than 0.5 from the golden.

KLD thresholds live per model in tests/golden/hw-gate/manifest.json (limits). The defaults are: - mean KLD at most 0.01; - KLD p99 at most 0.2; - the same top token at least 95% of the time.

A rerun at the recording pin gives 0 on every one.

The placement check reuses engine #390's report. The kat server runs with GGML_HRX_REPORT=2 (one line per graph) and -lv 4 (llama-server drops the library's INFO lines below it), and with GGML_HRX_STRICT=0, so a node off HRX is counted rather than aborting the server and losing the kat. tools/hw_gate_manifest.py placement then reads the server log the way serve does:

placement_observer: placement: 512 nodes, 0 off HRX (none), 1 graph splits

Any graph with a node off HRX fails the check, with the worst graph's counts and op types (20 of 354 nodes off HRX (MUL_MAT x 20), 5 graph splits; 1 of 41 graphs had nodes off HRX). A log with no report at all fails too: the check saw nothing. With --phases placement alone the server answers one short chat request instead of the kat, so a prompt graph and decode graphs are scheduled. The judge's verdicts are in tests/hw_gate_test.py (ctest hw_gate_judges).

One test-backend-ops case is a known intermittent failure (KNOWN-ISSUES.md, engine#370: MUL_MAT(type_a=f32,type_b=f32,m=1,n=1,k=2048), about 1 run in 40). When that is the only failing case, the case runs alone three more times and the check passes if all three are clean; the summary says so.

Box etiquette#

The gate shares the box with other work. It takes the GPU nine times: once for all the ops, once for the fa-decode-q8 runs, and once per MODEL_TABLE row (the server for kat and the needle, then llama-perplexity for the KLD, in one hold). Before the first of them it takes the fleet's GPU token, ~/GPU-TOKEN: the file long GPU jobs (Hyperloom, agents' benchmark holds) write their name into while they own the GPU. The gate waits while another job holds it, up to HW_GATE_TOKEN_WAIT seconds (default 3600), logging the holder; then it writes hw-gate <run> pid <pid> <time> into it and removes it on exit, only if the content is still its own. A wait that times out fails the run with exit 2 and names the holder. Two gate runs on 2026-10-20 (#481) died with "server failed (rc 137)" while Hyperloom held the token and loaded models of its own. Hyperloom's own token_take waits while a scripts/hw-gate.sh process exists, so the two take turns. HW_GATE_TOKEN=none skips the token for a caller that already holds it.

Each of those steps: - Lock. It holds ~/npu.lock (flock) only while it runs, so other GPU work keeps its turn between steps. - Heat. It waits for Tctl to drop to 75 C, then runs under ~/lb/thermal-run.sh, which freezes it at 78 C and kills it at 93 C. - Memory. It runs under scripts/mem-guard.sh (kills the step below 12 GB MemAvailable). Before a step starts, tools/mem_budget.py estimates it. A step that would take GTT to 95 GiB or more (the engine#315 fault zone), or past MemAvailable, is refused. The gate then releases the lock and retries every minute, up to ten times. - The PR-Agent model. coder-llm (Vulkan, :8090) loses its device when long HRX dispatches starve it. The gate runs on strixhalo-engine, the runner that also runs the pr-agent jobs, and a runner takes one job at a time, so no review is generating during the gate. Before each step the gate also waits for coder-llm's slots to be idle. Afterwards it reports any new ring ... timeout in the kernel log.

The build runs under thermal-run too, and resumes after a thermal kill. Build trees and ccache persist under ~/.cache/hw-gate, so a PR that does not move the pins rebuilds in seconds.

Goldens: where they live#

  • kat goldens are in git: tests/golden/hw-gate/kat-*.json. They are the text and per-token logprobs of every case, a few KB per model.
  • KLD base logits are not in git. They are 0.4-1.6 GB per model (llama-perplexity stores the whole vocabulary for every scored token), past GitHub's file limit, and only the gate box reads them. They live on that box under ~/.cache/hw-gate/kld/<model>.kld. tests/golden/hw-gate/manifest.json pins each one: its sha256, the model file fingerprint (size + sha256 of the first 64 MiB), the text's sha256, and the pins it was recorded at. The gate refuses a base, model or text that does not match. A private repository would add a token and a multi-GB download to every run for no gain while the gate has one box.

Record them again only at a release pin, after the gate passes there:

scripts/hw-gate.sh --phases build,kat,kld --record   # writes kat-*.json, the .kld files and manifest.json

and commit the changed tests/golden/hw-gate/ files in the same PR as the pin they belong to.

Running it by hand#

scripts/hw-gate.sh                                     # everything, on this checkout
scripts/hw-gate.sh --phases ops --models qwen3-0.6b    # a subset
scripts/hw-gate.sh --bin /path/to/llama.cpp/build/bin  # check binaries built elsewhere (no build)

The settings are environment variables at the top of the script: HW_GATE_STORE, HW_GATE_MODELS, HW_GATE_LOCK, HW_GATE_OPS, HW_GATE_MEM_FLOOR and the others. Logs and summary.md go to $HW_GATE_OUT (default ~/.cache/hw-gate/runs/<time>). Exit code: 0 pass, 1 a check failed, 2 the box could not run the gate (lock timeout, a model or base file missing, memory refused).

Measured#

Strix Halo, 2026-10-12, at the release pin (main d2a56a4, llama.cpp 0e255d77, hrx-system 98d05d94), on a box shared with about ten other GPU jobs:

step holds the GPU lock
build, incremental (no pin change) 6 s, no lock
build, cold (llama.cpp + hrx-system, 4 cores under thermal-run) about 20 min, no lock
ops: 611/611 cases pass 269 s
Qwen3-0.6B: kat (3 repeats) + needle 67 s
ZAYA1-8B: kat (2 repeats) 172 s
Qwen3.8-27B: kat (2 repeats) 213 s
KLD: 0.6B / 8B / 27B, 4,096 tokens each 6 / 24 / 29 s

That is about 13 minutes of GPU time in all.

Strix Halo, 2026-10-20, performance power mode, main 55929b5 (llama.cpp 00f2a68d, hrx-system 82804197) plus this coverage change, a quiet box (3 s waiting in all):

step holds the GPU lock
ops: 611/611 cases pass 20 s
Qwen3-0.6B: kat + needle + KLD 20 s
ZAYA1-8B: kat + needle + KLD (the needle: 7,421-token prompt at 1,207 tok/s, about 8 s) 70 s
Qwen3.8-27B: kat + KLD 184 s
Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B (MoE): kat + KLD 38 s
Qwen3-4B IQ4_XS: kat + KLD 31 s

363 s of GPU time in all; the MoE model, the IQ model and the ZAYA1 needle add about 77 s of it. Waiting for ~/npu.lock costs more than the gate itself: flock is not first-come-first-served, and with about ten jobs queueing, each acquisition waited 10 to 60 minutes. The summary reports both numbers (waiting, holding).

What the goldens record at the release pin: - Qwen3-0.6B misses one short needle (varied-720w: "25"). The check holds that case to the golden's text instead of the answer. - On varied-1620w, the cached path answers differently from a fresh request at a near-tie: top-2 margin 0.19, a WARN. - ZAYA1-8B and Qwen3.8-27B answer every case.

The MoE and IQ rows (qwen3-coder-30b-a3b, qwen3-4b-iq4xs) were recorded on 2026-10-20 at llama.cpp 00f2a68d / hrx-system 82804197 (manifest.json recorded_at). Both answer every kat case. Their HRX base logits against a CPU run of the same file (--device none) give:

model mean KLD KLD p99 same top token
Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Q4_K_M 0.0054 0.043 96.7%
Qwen3-4B IQ4_XS 0.0054 0.057 96.4%
Qwen3-0.6B Q4_K_M (the release-pin base, for comparison) 0.0080 0.039 95.8%

That is the usual GPU-vs-CPU rounding gap of a 4-bit file, not a wrong kernel.

Not covered yet#

  • Lock fairness. ~/npu.lock is a plain flock, so a job that re-queues quickly can starve the gate for an hour. A first-come-first-served queue, or a reserved window for the gate, would bound the wall time. The gate's own GPU time is 6 to 13 minutes.
  • Not exercised: 1bit serve itself (the gate talks to llama-server with serve's HRX flags), --parallel, --mtp / --dflash, vision, and contexts past 8K.
  • One copy of the KLD bases on the box. A spare copy of the release-pin set is on ryzen ~/backups/hw-gate-kld-0e255d77; the MoE and IQ bases are in ~/backups/hw-gate-kld-00f2a68d.
  • An intermittent bug that fires about once in 40 runs (#370's class) can pass a single gate run. kat repeats every case and the ops step re-runs a known flake, but only repeated runs catch such a bug reliably.
